title: No Keys at the Door
concept: Session Manager reaches a managed instance over the connection its own SSM Agent opens, so the instance needs no inbound port, no public address, no bastion host and no SSH key, and nothing has to change when an administrator's address does.

narration.text: No Keys at the Door, Pé na Areia. After last week's breach the shop's admin, in the hat, needs a shell on Web server A to read its logs, and the hooded Cloudling is probing for SSH on port 22. The web servers have only private addresses. Fly and see what each of them finds.

Neither got in. Nothing in the sky has a public address, so the probe had nowhere to knock, and the load balancer carries only HTTPS, never SSH. Safe, but the admin has no way in either. The usual answer is a bastion host.

A bastion host is a small instance with a public address, in a public subnet: the admin connects to it by SSH, then on to the private server. Drag the bastion host from the tray into Public subnet A, then fly.

edge-acl stopped both kites: it has no rule for SSH. On a public subnet's card, give edge-acl two rules: inbound, allow SSH from the operator's address; outbound, allow SSH to the VPC, for the hop on to the web server. Then fly.

Past edge-acl, the bastion's own security group, bastion-sg, turned the admin away: a new security group starts with no inbound rules. On the bastion's card, allow SSH from the operator's address only. Then fly.

The admin is on the bastion, but Web server A refused the hop: ec2-app-sg lets in only HTTP from the load balancer. On a web server's card, allow SSH from bastion-sg, the bastion's security group. Then fly.

The admin has a shell. Count what it took: a public machine to keep patched, four rules naming SSH and a private key to keep safe. And the hooded Cloudling is still knocking at the bastion: one leaked key, or one rule too wide, and it is in.
This weekend the admin is working from the coast, on a beach café's connection, with a new address. Nothing else has changed. Fly again.

Locked out: every rule names the old address. This is where people widen the rule to anywhere, just for today, and today lasts for years. Session Manager needs no open port at all, so there is no address to keep up with.

Drag Session Manager from the tray into the high band. The admin will ask Systems Manager for a session, and the session runs over a connection the instance itself opens: its SSM Agent's, out to Systems Manager on HTTPS 443.

Session Manager reaches only managed instances: ones whose SSM Agent has registered with Systems Manager, using the instance's role. On app-role's card, add: allow ssm:ManagedInstance on Session Manager.

The agent still needs a way out: the private route table reaches only S3. Drag a NAT Gateway into Public subnet B, then on a private subnet's card add the route Internet (0.0.0.0/0) to the NAT Gateway. Then fly.

The agent's connection crossed edge-acl, because the NAT Gateway sits behind it, and network ACLs are stateless. On edge-acl add outbound: HTTPS to anywhere; and inbound: ephemeral ports from anywhere, for the replies. Then fly.
A session, and no inbound port. Now close the door: remove the bastion host, then every rule that still mentions SSH, on edge-acl and on ec2-app-sg. Then fly.

No keys at the door: no open port, no bastion, no key to lose and no address to keep up with. IAM decides who may start a session, and [CloudTrail records each one](card:cloudtrail). No third star? A rule still mentions SSH. What a real account adds: [Session Manager in the real world](card:session-manager-real-world).

objectives.text: Every visitor is answered: orders found, receipts stored
The operator gets a shell through Session Manager
No security group lets SSH (port 22) in

wellArchitected.text: No keys at the door: no bastion host, and no security group or network ACL rule anywhere mentions SSH (port 22)

hints.nudge: Click a visitor who was turned away and follow its kite: which check stopped it?

pointer.text: The visitors need what Level 8 left: HTTPS through edge-acl and the load balancer, and the app role's permissions for the bucket and its key.

hints.nearAnswer: Undo the last change that touched edge-acl, ec2-app-sg or app-role, and fly again.

hints.nudge: Session Manager needs three things: to be in the sky, an instance that is managed, and a way out for the SSM Agent.

pointer.text: A managed instance's role allows ssm:ManagedInstance. Its agent reaches Systems Manager on HTTPS 443, through a NAT Gateway and back through edge-acl.

hints.nearAnswer: Place Session Manager; allow ssm:ManagedInstance on Session Manager in app-role; add a NAT Gateway in Public subnet B with the private route 0.0.0.0/0 to it; on edge-acl allow HTTPS out to anywhere and ephemeral ports in from anywhere.

hints.nudge: Which security groups still have a rule for SSH 22?

pointer.text: Look at bastion-sg and ec2-app-sg. A rule naming a security group that no longer exists goes when you remove it.

hints.nearAnswer: Remove the bastion host, and remove ec2-app-sg's rule allowing SSH from bastion-sg.
